component: P16 edge, packet, ROS-status and stateless lifecycle assurance refresh
constraints: Offline synthetic conformance must observe the actual published producer and verifier APIs, independently of structural acceptance or sensor-content validity.
Edge structure uses local references only; packet and ROS fixtures are source-pinned. Preserve distinct verifier UTC and scene/host clocks, UNKNOWN outcomes and absent rejection metadata.
Lifecycle observations must demonstrate caller rewind and protection from independently supplied floors without claiming persistence, restart or whole-store rollback protection.
No target hardware, memory budget, latency SLA or deployment runtime is selected by these small developer test drivers.
alternatives: Python unittest direct actual-API calls and language-neutral JSON fixtures; local python-jsonschema registry for the edge structural observation.
Java/Kotlin JUnit orchestration through a separate implementation adapter.
Robot Framework keyword orchestration through the published Python APIs.
Rust proptest for generated and shrunk input cases through an implementation boundary.
TLA+ or Alloy models and Erlang PropEr stateful generated tests for lifecycle exploration.
rationale: Edge consumer KEEP: three current methods independently validate the fixed UNKNOWN structure and authenticate bytes. Direct verifier observation is decisive; structural tools alone cannot authenticate. A foreign driver still requires an implementation adapter.

Packet/encoding consumer KEEP: seven methods call the published decoder and binding API separately, retaining authentic malformed content and missing depth. Proptest offers additional generated coverage, not a replacement decoder. No material native migration benefit is established for these fixed observations.

ROS consumer KEEP: three methods observe exact receipt/loss/fault statuses from the actual producer without copying its state machine. Keyword or JVM orchestration does not extend that fixed boundary. No live ROS/DDS deployment is inferred.

Lifecycle KEEP: two current traces call the real verifier with caller rewind and retained floors; both fail when the respective stronger floor is bypassed. Modeling tools complement actual-call observations but cannot establish them by themselves.

Fresh 24-method execution, four controlled substitutions with nine expected assertion failures, and seventeen producer-source comparisons supply bounded executable evidence. No new runtime or assertion mismatch was demonstrated.
Choices derive from actual API observability and explicit test scope, not installation, familiarity, incumbent language or rewrite cost. No alternative implementation was benchmarked or executed.
limits: These four KEEP decisions apply only to developer assurance harnesses, not future deployed components. Current evidence does not complete the assigned P16-P19 scope.
No model checker, full matrix, clean clone, distribution installation, physical hardware, timing, MLS/CNSA, availability or customer acceptance qualification was performed.
Selected source hashes do not establish atomic snapshots, loaded-code attestation, complete dependencies or authentic provenance. Local raw logs are not published release artifacts.
CI snapshot showed queued checks and one skip; no relevant exact-head PASS or merge. Earlier negative evidence remains intact.
